question: Under sensing conditions never used to design either tier, does the formal tier make fewer wrong refutations than the rule tier?

methods.formal: PAL v2.3 (eps 1e-3, nominal model, worst-case weather)
methods.rule: Rule k3 = ObjList-strict-moto (k=3, 1 m gate, liveness, any in-zone detection blocks, no motorcycle refutation)

H1: wrong refutations of genuine claims pooled over G1-G4, formal vs rule, exact two-sided McNemar, alpha 0.05, single test
H2: standard tier (both refute): Wilson 95% upper limit of wrong-refutation rate < 0.1%
secondary: error-coverage curves (eps 1e-1..1e-6; rule k 2..6, motorcycle rule on/off), matched-coverage comparison, per-condition counts without tests
reporting: all results reported regardless of outcome; conservative tier excluded (exploratory)
pre_freeze_change: window-end check made tolerant of the clock bound (v2.2 -> v2.3) after the clock0.3 sweep showed coverage 24%; checked on 400 sweep scenes (seeds 8,000,000+i) only

amendments.what: sim.py crashed in G3 (fabricated in-lane claimant drawn from uniform(d_max+8, 60) with d_max up to 72 m). Upper bound now d_max+20 when d_max+8 >= 60; identical draws whenever d_max+8 < 60, i.e. in every earlier condition and in G1, G2, G4. Made before any G3/G4 result existed; G1 and G2 results (already written) were not inspected.
